question: When should you finetune a foundation model, and which memory-efficient techniques (PEFT, LoRA, quantization, model merging) and hyperparameters make finetuning practical?
contributions: Framework for finetune vs RAG: finetuning is for form, RAG is for facts
Memory math for inference and training, numerical formats and quantization
Overview of PEFT, deep dive on LoRA and QLoRA, model merging, and finetuning tactics

limits: The chapter says finetuning needs data, ML talent and maintenance, and that new base models can overtake a finetuned one.
Model merging techniques are called experimental and may become outdated.
Written 2024; the author says LoRA does not match full finetuning performance and focuses on attention-matrix LoRA, which later work revised.

Many tables are reproduced from other papers (Ovadia, Li, Hu, Ma, Dettmers); the chapter runs no experiments except a count of >1,000 open issues in huggingface/peft in October 2024 as a popularity proxy.
Chapter covers SFT-style and adapter finetuning; preference finetuning/RL is only mentioned in the overview (format: instruction, winning response, losing response).
practices: Try prompting first, with systematic prompt experiments, before finetuning (When to Finetune).
Use finetuning for form and RAG for facts; if both kinds of failure exist, start with RAG, beginning with term-based search such as BM25 (Finetuning and RAG).
Workflow: prompt, add 1-50 examples, add RAG, then choose embedding retrieval or finetuning by failure mode, then combine both; evaluate at every step (Finetuning and RAG).
If a finetuned model loses ability on other tasks, finetune on all tasks, use separate models, or merge them (Reasons Not to Finetune).
Use LoRA first, attempt full finetuning later; with a few hundred examples full finetuning may not beat LoRA (Finetuning methods).
Start with the most powerful model you can afford, then follow the progression path or the distillation path from OpenAI's guidance (Base models).
Load a model in the numerical format it was intended for, e.g. BF16 for Llama 2 (Numerical Representations).
For multi-LoRA serving keep adapters separate; for a single LoRA model merge weights before serving (Serving LoRA adapters).
Choose alpha so alpha:r is typically between 1:8 and 8:1, and tune the pair (LoRA configurations).
Raise the learning rate as high as the loss curve stays stable; use gradient accumulation when memory forces small batches (Finetuning hyperparameters).
Prune task-vector parameters (TIES, DARE) before merging, more so with more models (Pruning redundant task-specific parameters).

terms.definition: how to transfer the knowledge gained from one task to accelerate learning for a new, related task
parameter-efficient finetuning; achieves performance close to full finetuning while using several orders of magnitude fewer trainable parameters
Low-Rank Adaptation; decomposes a weight matrix update into the product of two smaller matrices A and B, updated while W is frozen, then merged back
stores weights in 4-bit NF4 and dequantizes to BF16 for forward and backward pass, with paged optimizers
reducing precision; converting a model from a format with more bits to one with fewer
creating a custom model by combining multiple models, typically by mixing parameters (summing, layer stacking, concatenation)
the finetuned model minus the base model; captures the essence of the task; also called delta parameters
recomputing activations when needed instead of storing them; also called activation recomputation
accumulating gradients across several batches and updating weights once
continuous trainable vectors fed alongside input tokens, not human-readable
